prompt_payload.task: Design a diverse library of executable semantic optimization skills for finite-pool scientific search. Each skill defines interpretable rule features plus a conservative Bayesian linear surrogate blended with strong target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI anchors.

target.title: MoleculeNet FreeSolv hydration free-energy replay
target.boundary: Field values and counts are public; target outcomes are not included.

source_transfer_evidence.boundary: No source identity, source schema, source outcomes, source effects, or source value priors are provided. The LLM must use the public target schema and its pretrained domain knowledge only.

executor.semantic_model: Rules become binary features. Revealed target outcomes fit a ridge Bayesian linear surrogate whose coefficient prior follows rule weights.
executor.anchor: A rank blend of target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI.
executor.fusion: semantic_mass_start/end controls the rank mass assigned to the semantic surrogate; the remaining mass stays on the target-only anchor.
executor.selection: Independent calibration seeds select one frozen skill. Independent held-out seeds are evaluated only after selection.

design_requirements: Use only exact field/value pairs in public_semantic_fields.

Each conditions object must map a real catalog field name directly to one exact catalog value, for example {"dominant_family": "oxide"}. Never use literal placeholder keys such as exact_field, field_name, field, or value.
Give every skill a distinct, descriptive scientific skill_id. Never copy schema placeholders such as short_unique_name or add numeric suffixes to a placeholder.
Give every skill 3-10 rules; use two-condition interactions only when scientifically meaningful.
Include at least one conservative low-semantic-mass skill.
Use only target-schema-compatible domain knowledge; do not imply that a source task or source outcomes were observed.
Include at least one domain-knowledge skill.
Include a counter-hypothesis skill that reverses or downweights an uncertain source relation.
Prefer mechanistic, chemically or physically interpretable rules over arbitrary coverage rules.
Use positive weights for conditions expected to improve the target objective and negative weights for risks.
Do not claim access to target outcomes and do not output candidate identifiers.

rules.rationale: short scientific rationale

skills.hypothesis: what this skill transfers and when it may fail

cards.title: FreeSolv to Lipophilicity transferable skill
cards.summary: A molecular-property transferable skill instance using shared SMILES-derived descriptor fields as the representation bridge.
cards.content: Representation mapping: shared descriptor bins such as smiles_length_bin, hetero_atom_bin, halogen_bin, aromatic_bin, ring_token_bin, branch_bin, and double_bond_bin transfer directly because the source and target adapters use the same public vocabulary. Mechanism hypothesis: coarse SMILES-derived structure descriptors can indicate reusable molecular-property search geometry across hydration free energy and lipophilicity tasks. Model binding: transfer-card role confidence reweights the categorical GP kernel. Acquisition binding: GP-UCB remains the selector. Gate/risk boundary: value-level transfer is only allowed for shared descriptor vocabularies; dataset-local labels should not be transferred this way. Current 50-seed result: GP-UCB final_best 88.4775 / AUC 86.4578; transfer_weighted_gp_ucb_scale_1p5 final_best 88.5650 / AUC 86.6808.

cards.title: Reusable semantic feature pattern: high_aromatic_content
cards.summary: For real_moleculenet_lipophilicity, use the LLM to define the high_aromatic_content feature partition, then fit its direction and magnitude from revealed target observations.
cards.content: Evidence mode: target_only. Execution: disabled. Reusable lesson: preserve the LLM-proposed feature partition, but calibrate or remove unsupported coefficient signs before held-out evaluation.

care_knowledge_context.instruction: Use these public, previously archived cards only as reusable design lessons. Do not copy reported target values into a rule and do not imply that the current target outcomes were observed. Prefer lessons that survived held-out calibration.

rules.rationale: Low heteroatom count may correlate with favorable hydration free energy due to reduced polarity and simpler solvation shell.
Absence of halogens avoids strong, localized dipole moments that can disrupt water network formation.
Non-aromatic molecules may have more conformational flexibility, aiding in entropy-driven favorable hydration.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the hypothesis that simple, non-polar, flexible molecules exhibit higher hydration affinity. May fail for molecules where specific polar interactions or aromatic stacking are critical.

rules.rationale: Low aromaticity combined with low halogen content may balance hydrophobic and mild polar contributions for optimal solvation.
Few rings reduce molecular rigidity, potentially increasing favorable entropy upon hydration.
Low branching simplifies molecular surface, possibly leading to more predictable water structure.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the hypothesis that balanced aromatic and halogen features, with low structural complexity, promote hydration affinity. May fail for molecules where specific halogen-aromatic interactions are detrimental.

rules.rationale: Short SMILES strings often correspond to smaller molecules, which may have less unfavorable hydrophobic surface area.
Absence of double bonds reduces electron density and potential for unfavorable polar interactions with water.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers minimal semantic bias towards small, saturated molecules, heavily relying on the target-only anchor. May fail if critical molecular features for hydration are omitted.

rules.rationale: High heteroatom count increases polarity, potentially leading to strong, ordered water shells with unfavorable entropy.
High halogen content introduces strong dipoles and possible halogen bonding, which can disrupt bulk water structure.
High branching creates complex molecular surfaces, potentially leading to heterogeneous and unfavorable hydration.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the hypothesis that high polarity and structural complexity are detrimental to hydration affinity. May fail for molecules where specific polar groups form favorable direct interactions with water.

rules.rationale: No rings maximize conformational flexibility, increasing the entropy gain upon release of ordered water molecules.
Low double bond count reduces rigidity and planarity, favoring entropically favorable hydration.
Medium-sized molecules balance sufficient hydrophobic surface for driving force without excessive ordering penalty.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers physical chemistry domain knowledge that entropy is a major driver for hydration free energy. May fail for enthalpy-dominated systems where specific polar interactions are crucial.

rules.rationale: Downweights the common assumption that low aromaticity is always beneficial; aromatic rings may provide favorable hydrophobic interactions.
Moderate heteroatom count may offer optimal balance for both enthalpic and entropic contributions.
Moderate ring count may provide structural stability without excessive rigidity.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers a counter-hypothesis that moderate aromaticity and heteroatom content can be beneficial, challenging simple polarity-averse rules. May fail if the dataset strongly favors extremely non-polar molecules.

rules.rationale: No branching leads to linear or simple cyclic structures, minimizing surface complexity and promoting uniform hydration.
Short molecules have low molecular weight, often associated with less hydrophobic surface and favorable hydration.
Saturated bonds reduce electronic polarization and potential for specific, unfavorable water interactions.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the hypothesis that maximal structural simplicity (no branches, short, saturated) maximizes hydration affinity. May fail for molecules where some complexity is needed for optimal hydrophobic packing.

rules.rationale: Combination of low heteroatoms and no halogens strongly indicates low polarity, favorable for hydrophobic hydration.
Absence of aromatics and few rings maximizes flexibility and minimizes planar hydrophobic surfaces.
Low branching and few double bonds reduce both steric and electronic complexity.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the hypothesis that synergistic combinations of low-complexity features across multiple descriptors best predict high hydration affinity. May fail if non-additive or specific functional group effects dominate.
